descriptor.scene: Maya is the subject, mid-work on delivery day: with her right hand she lifts a light timber scaffold strut away from around her engine, her closed silver laptop still under her left arm, her expression glad and unsentimental. The engine is brand NEW, freshly arrived, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the same waist-high cream machine, dial upright, calm warm hum lines, still sitting beside the pale-wood delivery crate it arrived in, a small round cream parachute of plain cloth draped half-folded over the crate's edge. Around the engine, the old scaffolding is coming down on purpose: a few struts still standing, and the removed struts stacked NEATLY in a tidy pile at the side, ends aligned. Her young tower rises solid at the edge of frame behind her. Warm midday light, the mood of good housekeeping, not demolition. Her full figure reads a little under half the frame height. The lower right of the frame stays calm grass beside the neat strut pile.
negatives: two engines in frame (the old engine is already gone; only the new one)
a compass, or anything inside or spilling from the crate (the crate is the engine's own delivery crate, already empty)
the scaffolding collapsed, thrown down or scattered (removed struts are stacked neatly)
lettering or stencils on the crate or parachute
descriptor._caption: Every season, the keepers send down a better engine. Maya's first job on delivery day is deletion. Half her scaffolding existed to steady the old engine, and the new one does not need it. Guardrails are built for the machine you had. She takes them down on purpose, the day the new machine arrives.
